issues.description: unresolved-items.json is procedure-body-scoped: UnresolvedItemAggregator.Build is fed only navigationGraph + functionClassifications (Pipeline.cs:612-614), and FunctionClassificationBuilder walks only procedure bodies, so unresolved references in procedure headers (proven reproducer: `Public Sub Demo(Optional ByVal x As Variant = MissingThing)` -> 1 unresolved in Body.References, 0 in the aggregated index) and at module level (Implements/Private As New/Const initializers) are dropped from the run-wide index. It is therefore not a structural superset of Body.References[ResolutionStatus=Unresolved].
issues.verificationMethod: GPT-5.4 scratch-probe against the current assemblies (set-wide addendum C9); Gemini independently flagged the module-level manifestation. Orchestrator confirmed the production call args and the absence of any superset pin.
issues.suggestedTestOrCheck: Hermetic pin: parse `Public Sub Demo(Optional ByVal x As Variant = MissingThing)`, assert MissingThing appears in BOTH ParserOutput.Body.References AND the aggregated UnresolvedItems; add a module-level case.
issues.resolution_notes: DEFERRED to DW-11 (operator-adjudicated at closeout). Rationale: the correct fix carries a real design decision (avoid re-introducing the double-emit the original wiring deliberately avoided) and is golden-neutral on HHC, so it belongs in a focused, properly-verified session rather than a docs-scope closeout. Consumer risk bounded + disclosed: interpretation-guide §6 now documents the scoping caveat and points to the inline per-reference ResolutionReason as the authoritative COMPLETE signal. Proven reproducer captured in DW-11 as the owning session's first task.

issues.description: interpretation-guide §5.7 told consumers to join NavigationGraph.TargetName against a `Name` field on the manifest's Forms/Reports entries, and §4 described every per-category entry as a small `{ Name, ... }` record. Both are inaccurate: Forms entries are `{ Spec }` and Reports entries are `{ Spec, ParserOutput }` with the object name at Spec.SourceFormName (reports reuse that key); Modules use ModuleName; only Queries/Tables/Relationships carry a top-level Name. A consumer coding the join literally would look up a nonexistent property.
issues.verificationMethod: GPT-5.4 main-prompt C1 (PowerShell probe of the golden); orchestrator confirmed entry shapes across all six categories against samples/GoldenOutput/HomeHealthCare/manifest.json.
issues.resolution_notes: Fixed this session: §5.7 join sentence now points to Spec.SourceFormName / the ir/ filename stem and warns there is no top-level Name on Forms/Reports entries; §4 stub bullet rewritten to give the per-category name field accurately.

issues.description: Under the shared ProjectScope, a module that throws during pass-2 resolution (VBA_RESOLVE_FAILURE) is excluded from resolvedModules and ships as a ParserOutput=null stub, yet its pass-1 scope stays in the shared project, so a sibling can carry a `ResolutionStatus:Resolved` reference whose target shipped as a null-ParserOutput stub. A consumer dereferencing the target's body on the strength of the Resolved status could crash.
issues.verificationMethod: Gemini set-wide addendum C7(b) flagged the deref hazard; GPT-5.4 could find no live Resolve() throw path (only null-arg guards) so the state is reachable-by-contract but not currently triggerable. Orchestrator confirmed the exclude-but-keep-scope code path at Pipeline.cs:480-499.
issues.resolution_notes: Consumer-facing risk fixed via doc: interpretation-guide §4 now documents VBA_RESOLVE_FAILURE and instructs consumers to null-check a referenced module's ParserOutput regardless of the reference's resolved status. The latent code-side hardening (prune resolve-failed scopes / annotate the reference) is deferred as DW-12 (not currently triggerable).
